function: PPO agent jointly sets sensing/communication time split, UAV sensing power, CPU allocation and IoTD-UAV association to maximize service success and minimize energy (pp. 6-7).
system: 4 hovering UAVs at 120 m (antenna array, radar), 10 single-antenna IoT devices, time-division sensing and communication, no RIS, carrier frequency not given (pp. 3, 10).
method: PPO actor-critic (PBIA), fully connected 128x256x256 actor and 128x256x128 critic; reinforcement learning with asynchronous parallel server-worker training (pp. 7-10).
data_channel: Custom simulator: free-space path-loss gains (Eqs. 3, 7), Shannon rate, 400 m Manhattan block; no standard channel model or dataset (pp. 4-5, 10).
test_conditions: Trained up to 3000 episodes at 10 devices, 3 UAVs, 2 m/s; tested over 100 episodes; sweeps of devices, UAVs, speed, weights use separate training runs (pp. 10-13).
baselines: Non-learned: Random and Static (proximity association, proportional CPU, median values). Learned: DDPG and REINFORCE, same parallel training (p. 11).
metrics: Average reward, service success rate, system energy consumption (J), service delay (s), UAV load-balance metric, plus training convergence curves (pp. 11-12, Table III).
complexity: Training complexity order O1 in Lemma 1 (Eq. 39): episodes x steps x layer-width products of actor and critic; no runtime or FLOPs (p. 9).
openness: none (no code or data link; custom MATLAB simulation, p. 10).
q1_support: p. 5: "The channel power gain of the ground-to-air link" is a custom free-space expression (Eq. 7) in a simulated Manhattan block (p. 10); no 3GPP, QuaDRiGa, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is used or mentioned.
q2_support: p. 12: "the reward curve of the PBIA algorithm converges regardless of changes in the number of UAVs"; Figs. 7(a), 8(a), 9 (p. 13) are per-setting training curves and the state size 3m+4n (p. 7) changes with the setting, so each setting is retrained; no trained model is tested in an unseen setting.
q3_support: p. 11: "Random: All service decisions of UAVs are randomized" and "Static decisions: The service policy of UAVs is fixed"; p. 11: "DDPG: An off-policy DRL algorithm"; p. 12: "PBIA showcases substantial improvements ranging from 15.78% to 66.36% and 16.32% to 61.44%, respectively, compared to baselines" (Table III, reward and success rate).
q4_support: p. 9: "Lemma 1: The complexity of Algorithm 1 is O1", with O1 given in Eq. 39 from episodes, steps and layer widths of actor and critic (training complexity); no measured runtime or FLOPs.
q5_support: p. 10: "we utilized the Deep Learning, Reinforcement Learning, and Parallel Computing toolbox of MATLAB 2023b" for a custom simulator; the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public channel dataset.
notes: Borderline above_phy: the learned actions mix above-PHY decisions (service association, CPU allocation, time-slot scheduling) with UAV sensing-power control (Eq. 22, p. 7); included through the aerial-link clause (power control and resource allocation learned jointly with association). Area 5 also fits (sensing/communication time and power) but area 6 wins by the tie-break order. Antenna array of the UAV is not modelled beyond scalar gains (p. 4); Table II (p. 10) gives no carrier frequency. Reviewer should confirm that the sensing power and time split count as a physical-layer decision.
